q: You typed the project ID with a spelling mistake and created the project. What now?
o: Run firebase use to fix it
why: A project ID can never be changed after creation. The display name can change, the ID cannot.

q: A reviewer finds your web apiKey in public code. What is the right response?
o: It is fine; check rules are strict
why: The web config is public by design. Data is protected by security rules and App Check, not by hiding the key.

q: Which of these must never be shipped inside app code?
why: A service account key gives full admin power over the project. The config values only identify the project.

q: You run emulators:start and it fails with a Java error. What is the likely fix?
why: Some emulators are Java programs, and current CLI versions need Java 21 or later.

q: The Notes app needs photo uploads. Which plan does Cloud Storage need?
o: No plan, it is always free
why: Cloud Storage, including the default bucket, needs the Blaze plan. You can still test free in the Storage emulator.

q: Most of your users are in one country. When do you choose the Firestore location?
why: Firestore's location is set when the database is created and cannot be changed later, so choose one close to your users.

q: A budget alert on the Blaze plan stops all spending when the budget is reached.
why: Myth. A budget alert only sends a notification. It does not cap usage or charges.

q: On the Spark plan, passing a free quota stops that product until the quota resets, and you are not charged.
why: Fact. Spark never charges you; the product stops working for the project until the quota resets.
